The reference is legible where the two fields differ and near-invisible where they coincide.

rubric.data_ink: pass. Contour lines are the only data ink: 45683 retained px and 2819 charcoal px outside the legend glyphs, against 5039 black px that are the wall plus the dashed strokes. Nothing is shaded or filled except the null glyphs the repository's flux-map rule requires.

rubric.label_collision: pass. Zero non-white pixels in the outer 2 px frame of the 1400x1000 render, so no title or legend text is clipped; the four panel titles sit in their own shelves and the three legend columns do not touch.
rubric.legibility: pass. Four panels, each titled above it and drawn with axes off, over one frameless six-entry legend: 'retained field' (solid teal), 'reference field' (dashed charcoal), 'retained axis' (teal triangle), 'reference axis' (charcoal triangle), 'retained saddle' (teal cross), 'reference saddle' (charcoal cross). In the two diverted panels the retained and analytic fields visibly separate and the dashed reference reads clearly. Legend glyphs occupy one clean band near the bottom of the canvas and no glyph touches another.
rubric.table_form: pass. A 2x2 grid of poloidal flux maps with walls and null sets is a spatial relationship, not a table.

findings.evidence: SVG path styles: the axes_1..axes_4 paths carry 'stroke: #333333; stroke-dasharray: 8.88,3.84; stroke-width: 2.4'; the retained groups carry 'stroke: #1f6f8b; stroke-width: 2'. Pixel counts measured with PIL on final-terminal-preview.png.
findings.summary: The reference series is largely occluded by the retained series drawn over it, and the occluding line is the thinner one. Each panel draws the reference contours first (stroke #333333, dashed 8.88,3.84, width 2.4) and the retained contours after, on top (stroke #1f6f8b, solid, width 2.0), so where the two agree the reader sees one teal line with a dark dotted edge rather than two marks. On the run's 1400x1000 render only 2674 px of reference dash ink are visible against 45683 retained px, falling to 578 and 602 px in the two limited panels where the fields coincide, and the legend draws both series keys at 2.4 pt so the width hierarchy the reader sees is not the one the legend implies. A reader of the limited panels cannot recover the analytic contour positions independently; only the diverted panels, where the fields separate, let the reference be read on its own. This does not meet the blocking bar - the disagreement is visible exactly where it is nonzero, and the two series are separated by dash pattern as well as colour - but it is the figure's weakest reading and is recorded for the coordinator.

findings.evidence: docs/evidence/fragments/converged-forward-solve/read-correction-path.html line 24 (the figure element's alt and figcaption); reviewed manifest artifacts 'diverted2098 strict xfail 0.0262254747411'; final-render-terminal.log 'limited 550 retained' and 'limited 2000 retained' each x_points_drawn 0.
findings.summary: The figure's accessible alt text describes an artifact the render does not show, and the caption names one panel by a count its own title contradicts. The alt reads 'Four certified poloidal terminal states over analytic reference contours, with walls and both sets of magnetic axes and saddles', but the reviewed run's own receipt records the diverted 2,098-cell row as a strict xfail at residual 0.0262254747411 (not certified), and the render log records x_points_drawn 0 for all four limited reads, so no saddle is drawn in the two limited panels at all. The caption beneath is accurate and discloses both facts ('the diverted 2,000-cell panel shows its nonconverged terminal field'), so the defect is confined to the alt text, which is the only description a screen-reader user receives. The caption also calls the panel 'the diverted 2,000-cell panel' where the panel title reads 'Diverted, 2,098 cells', a nominal-versus-measured cell count that the title and the receipt both resolve to 2,098. No edit made (read-only review).

item_verdicts.caption_independence: The caption does not merely repeat the figure's title. The figure carries no title element (identity is in the file name and the per-panel shelf titles), and the caption states the render job and device, the two series and their styles, the shared level array per panel, that axes are off, and that the diverted panel is nonconverged. It is a description, not a restatement; its one inaccuracy, the '2,000-cell' name for the 'Diverted, 2,098 cells' panel, is recorded inside finding 2.
item_verdicts.finding_materiality: Two follow-on findings, no blocking finding. Nothing is clipped (zero frame ink), no label overlaps another label or the data, no text is unreadable, and the image is not tabular, so none of the blocking categories the rubric names is met. Finding 1 sits close to the blocking boundary and is stated with its measurements so the coordinator can judge it.
item_verdicts.rendered_artifact: The reviewed head's figure was opened as an image both as the run's own 1400x1000 preview (byte-identical SVG provenance) and as my own 4200x3000 render of the head blob, and inspected at native resolution and in 250-400 percent crops of three panels and the legend. No verdict below is read from the source file alone.

rubric_lines: RUBRIC legibility: pass. Four poloidal line-contour panels on one canvas, each titled in a shelf above it ('Limited, 553 cells', 'Limited, 2,105 cells', 'Diverted, 550 cells', 'Diverted, 2,098 cells'), axes off, with one frameless six-entry legend below the panels. The retained field reads as a teal line and the reference as charcoal dashes; the four terminal states are distinguishable at a glance. The occlusion of the reference series is recorded as finding 1 but does not stop a reader reading the figure.

RUBRIC data_ink: pass. Line contours only. Outside the legend the 1400x1000 render holds 45683 retained-teal px, 2819 charcoal px and 5039 black px, and the only solid fills are the required null-marker glyphs and the white page; no gradient, band or area fill is drawn.

RUBRIC decoration: pass. No gridlines, spine, tick, background fill or drop shadow; the axis furniture is off per the repository's poloidal rule. The white space in the top-left quadrant and beneath the panels is 2x2 grid layout, not decoration.

RUBRIC contrast: pass. Retained teal #1f6f8b is about 5.7:1 on white, reference charcoal #333333 about 12.6:1, the wall black about 21:1, and all title and legend text is near-black on white; every mark clears the 3:1 graphics floor, and the two contour series are additionally separated by dash pattern.

RUBRIC table_form: pass. Four spatially arranged poloidal flux maps with stationary points and a wall are a spatial relationship; the comparison the caption claims (retained against its analytic reference on shared per-panel levels) is what a contour overlay carries and a table would not.

RUBRIC label_collision: pass. Zero non-white pixels in the outer 2 px frame of the 1400x1000 render, so no title or legend text is clipped, and every title and legend entry occupies its own band. The overlapping null markers of finding 1 are markers, not labels.
